courses.name: Freshman Seminar for Computing
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces new Bellini College students to degree choices, academic requirements and support resources.

category_review.locator: CIS 1930 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The entire description is first-year orientation and academic navigation; it does not establish programming or other computing subject content.

courses.name: Programming Concepts
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces programming concepts and design methods through a contemporary programming language.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACT Math (min score 24) OR College Algebra MPT (min score 12) OR College-Level Math CPT (min score 60) OR SAT Math (min score 570); Course restrictions: Majors Only

category_review.locator: COP 2510 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The description expressly centers programming and software design.

courses.name: Composition I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces rhetorical analysis, audience-aware writing, composition processes and language conventions.
courses.prerequisites: Other information: Scores of: STI1 of 440 or TFL4 of 550 or TFIT of 079 or EAC1 of 17 or EAC3 of 18.

category_review.locator: ENC 1101 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Rhetoric and written communication are the explicit subjects.

courses.name: Calculus I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies single-variable limits, derivatives and integrals, with optimization and other applications.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 1147 (min grade C) OR SAT Math (min score 670) OR ACT Math (min score 29) OR College-Level Math CPT (min score 90) OR PreCalc & Trig MPT (min score 12); Other information: Knowledge of trigonometry.

category_review.locator: MAC 2311 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Calculus concepts and mathematical problem solving are explicit.

courses.name: Program Design
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Develops program design and construction using C in a networked environment.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 2510 (min grade B) AND MAC 2311 (min grade B); Course restrictions: Consent of Instructor or Department,Majors Only,Permit Required

category_review.locator: COP 3514 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Program construction is the central subject; a networked setting does not make this a networking-infrastructure course.

courses.name: Composition II
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Practices effective reading, writing and public speaking.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: ENC 1101 (min grade C-)

category_review.locator: ENC 1102 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The description centers human communication.

courses.name: Calculus II
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Develops integration, series and elementary transcendental functions for mathematical problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2311 OR MAC 2281 (min grade C); Other information: No credit for students with credit in MAC 2242 or MAC 2282.

category_review.locator: MAC 2312 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The description centers calculus and mathematical methods.

courses.name: General Physics I - Calculus Based
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces calculus-based mechanics, fluids, oscillations and waves for science and engineering students.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2281 OR MAC 2311 (both min grade C-); Co-prerequisites: PHY 2048L (min grade C-); Other information: Must be taken concurrently with lab and, if dropped, then dropped simultaneously. May not receive credit for both the PHY 2053 and PHY 2048 courses. Not repeatable.

category_review.locator: PHY 2048 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Physics is substantive domain knowledge; using calculus does not make the course mathematical theory or computing foundations.

courses.name: General Physics I Laboratory
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Provides the first laboratory in the two-semester general-physics sequence for physics and engineering students.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2281 OR MAC 2311 (both min grade C-); Co-prerequisites: PHY 2048 (min grade C-); Other information: Must be taken concurrently with lecture and, if dropped, then dropped simultaneously. May not receive credit for both the PHY 2053L and PHY 2048L courses.

category_review.locator: PHY 2048L Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Experimental physics is the stated domain practice; the whole sequence topic list is not a claim that this laboratory alone covers every listed topic.

courses.name: Computer Organization
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces digital hardware, processor organization, memory and I/O, with computer arithmetic and assembly programming.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 2510 (min grade B) AND PHY 2048 (min grade B); Course restrictions: Consent of Instructor or Department,Majors Only

category_review.locator: CDA 3103 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: Computer architecture and hardware organization dominate the description.

courses.name: Introduction to Discrete Structures

courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2311 (min grade C)

category_review.locator: COT 3100 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The actual description centers mathematical structures and logic, rather than implementing data structures or algorithms.

courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies and implements data structures for clear, efficient programs, including functional-programming concepts.

category_review.locator: COP 4530 Course Details: full description
category_review.rationale: The description centers data structures, representations and programming.

requirements.summary: A waiver may be requested for documented seasonal summer employment in each summer missed, unavailable program courses certified by an advisor, or exceptional hardship outside the student’s control. Submit supporting evidence during the graduation-application semester; allow three weeks for a decision. A request is not automatic approval.

requirements.title: Grade-forgiveness limits
requirements.summary: Both attempts must be at USF; the repeat grade must be at least D. At most three forgiveness uses are allowed, with one repeat per course. Academic-dishonesty FF grades are excluded, and forgiveness cannot change courses counted toward an already awarded bachelor’s degree. This does not establish AI-major passing grades.

requirements.title: Civic-literacy entry cohorts
requirements.summary: Complete applicable civic literacy before graduation. The entry date at a Florida public institution controls: before Summer B 2018 generally exempt; Summer B 2018–Summer A 2021 requires course or assessment; Summer B 2021 onward requires both. Out-of-state and additional-degree students are not categorically exempt; the FAQ requires returning earlier graduates to fulfill previously unmet civic literacy.

requirements.title: Approved course and assessment routes
requirements.summary: Course options are POS 2041, AMH 2020, AMH 2010 completed Fall 2024 onward, or transfer-only AMS X010 from Fall 2024 onward. Assessment uses FCLE or approved acceleration. The internal USF Canvas test is available only to pre-Fall-2024 entrants and requires 60%, with unlimited attempts.

requirements.title: Civic transfer and prior assessment evidence
requirements.summary: Florida public-college/university credit needs official transcript evidence for each completed component; an incomplete component remains due. A high-school FCLE pass of at least 60% needs the official transcript and satisfies assessment only. Out-of-state course substitutions require an advisor-submitted syllabus review.

requirements.title: General-education overlap and passing grade
requirements.summary: POS X041, AMH X010 and AMH X020 may also meet state-core social science with C− or better. A lower passing grade may satisfy civic literacy alone. AMH X010 must be completed Fall 2024 onward. Naturalization testing does not satisfy the assessment.

requirements.title: Approved acceleration mechanisms
requirements.summary: Both components: AP US Government ≥3, AP US History ≥4, CLEP American Government ≥50, or CLEP US History I ≥50. Course only: AICE US History A-level A–E, CLEP US History II ≥50, IB History of the Americas 5–7, or passing approved dual enrollment (Fall 2024 timing applies to AMH X010/AMS X010).

requirements.title: Statewide course-equivalency framework
requirements.summary: SCNS equivalence ordinarily requires the same prefix/last three digits, comparable faculty credentials and the applicable minimum grade; equivalent transferred work serves requirements on the same basis as native credit. Quarter and semester amounts may differ. Other credit acceptance remains institution-specific.

requirements.title: Exceptions to automatic course equivalency
requirements.summary: Individual review applies to unoffered or unaccredited/pre-transfer-date courses; 900–999 special work; adult applied academics; graduate courses; internships, apprenticeships, practica, clinical or abroad experiences; and performing-art/Criminal Justice skill courses. These exceptions do not establish approval for an AI requirement.

requirements.title: First-year entry and preparation
requirements.summary: Bellini first-year entry is in fall or spring. AI applicants need a strong record including four years of advanced mathematics and science including chemistry and physics; additional preparatory coursework may be necessary. University admission does not remove program-specific catalog conditions.

requirements.title: Math placement and prior calculus credit
requirements.summary: New first-year students must pass basic and college algebra placement; prior high-school precalculus/calculus adds the precalculus/trigonometry exam. Each passing score is 12 of 15. Passing all three supports starting Calculus I in fall; existing Calculus I credit is exempt. The page’s reference to students unable to complete “the course” does not identify a blanket placement-failure dismissal rule.

requirements.title: Transfer admission level
requirements.summary: Lower-level transfer means 12–29 prior postsecondary credit hours, mid-level 30–59, and upper-level at least 60. These are admission cohorts, not undergraduate course levels.

requirements.title: AI lower-level transfer admission
requirements.summary: Require (SAT mathematics at least 570 OR ACT mathematics at least 24) AND high-school GPA at least 4.00 as calculated by Admissions. This is the explicitly shared Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence entry rule.

requirements.title: AI mid/upper-level programming admission prerequisite
requirements.summary: Complete Programming Concepts via COP 1220, COP 2030, COP 2224, COP 2360, COP 2510 or COP 2800 with at least C within at most two attempts. Transfer alternatives are not asserted to be six current USF offerings or six degree requirements.

requirements.title: AI mid/upper-level mathematics and physics entry prerequisites
requirements.summary: Complete Calculus I (MAC x281 or MAC x311), Calculus II (MAC x282 or MAC x312), and calculus-based Physics I with lab (PHY x048/PHY x048L or PHY x045/PHY x045L), each with at least C within at most two attempts. Wildcard codes remain as printed. The following Computer Engineering chemistry requirement and Cybersecurity/IT database, statistics and discrete-mathematics requirements do not apply through this AI section.

requirements.title: Accelerated credit documentation
requirements.summary: AP, IB, AICE, CAPE and dual-enrollment credit require official documents submitted to Admissions. Consult advising before retaking previously credited coursework; acceptance does not by itself establish AI requirement allocation.

requirements.title: Transfer acceptance versus degree allocation
requirements.summary: Admissions assesses transfer acceptance and recalculates GPA using all submitted transcripts. A transfer-credit summary does not establish allocation to degree requirements and excludes coursework still in progress when the transcript arrived.

requirements.title: College and department allocation of transferred work
requirements.summary: Out-of-state/private-institution courses are not guaranteed to satisfy either general education or major requirements. Departments review them individually; colleges determine degree applicability. Retain official course descriptions and syllabi. Degree Works allocation remains provisional until reviewed by advising or college personnel. This is a conditional approval procedure, not evidence that every proposed substitution is permitted.

requirements.title: Public advising and authenticated forms

requirements.title: Completion and university-initiated graduation
requirements.summary: Once degree requirements are complete, graduation occurs within the university’s four-year progression framework; the university may initiate graduation certification without a student application.

requirements.title: Added work and primary-major completion term
requirements.summary: Additional curricular and co-curricular work must finish by the primary-major completion term, normally eight semesters excluding summer and alternative terms. Transfer progression counting includes prior postsecondary enrollment; this is not a promise of eight additional USF semesters.

requirements.title: Enrollment after six active postsecondary terms
requirements.summary: After six active postsecondary terms, enrollment is restricted to courses needed for the primary declared major. Student-specific exceptions require the documented policy process.

requirements.title: Major change and academic progression
requirements.summary: Receiving-college approval and progression/excess-credit review apply to major changes; changes after drop/add take effect the next term. Colleges may reselect students who fail progression. Specific major standards remain in the catalog.

requirements.title: Documented progression exceptions
requirements.summary: Submit written exception documentation to the Dean of Undergraduate Studies before applying to graduate. Extensions are not granted to retake already satisfactory graduation courses or prepare for graduate admission.
